#2

eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business

eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business

1147 分 739 评论 最高 #2 10 次快照出现
  • Will Sharpen Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS BENGALURU, INDIA, October 22, 2026 - eMudhra Limited (BSE: 543533 | NSE: EMUDHRA), a global digital trust company, today announced that its Board has decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business. Mr. V. Srinivasan, Chairman, eMudhra Limited referred to the recent incident relating to its global SSL/TLS certificate and indicated that eMudhra handled the recent incident diligently, revoking the affected CAs within 14 hours of discovery and disclosing promptly. There were no end entity certificates issued out of the affected CA’s. Its infrastructure was not compromised and no data was breached. All physical and logical security controls remained intact. He added that global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1% of the global revenue. Due to increasing data sovereignty & compliance requirements, complexity and cost associated with this business is increasing over the years. This, paired with the fact that some of the large entities issue the SSL/TLS free of cost, the business potential and RoI of this line of business also has considerably reduced for eMudhra when measured against our cumulative revenue base. However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business. In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders. For many certifying authorities, SSL/TLS is the whole business. For eMudhra it is one part of a much broader digital solutions portfolio. We will put our energy where we create the most value for customers with Sharpened Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS. Seamless transition for customers Our G1 RSA roots will continue to serve customers until this transition is complete as we work with browser programs and our customers to enable this transition. eMudhra will reach out to affected customers to replace any certificate free of cost from partners through the transition. Revocation and certificate status services will keep running until every issued certificate has expired or been replaced. eMudhra will complete its remaining commitments to the browser root programs, including a full root-cause report. Core businesses unaffected eMudhra’s global SSL/TLS infrastructure runs separately from its other operations. The company’s Global digital signature certificate (DSC), eSign, and other signing services, including those in India, its enterprise PKI Solutions (emCA, CertiNext platforms), emSigner eSignature Suite, and its identity and authentication solutions (SecurePass, emAS) are not affected and continue to operate as normal. About eMudhra With over 17 years of expertise, eMudhra is a global provider of digital identity, trust, and security solutions, enabling secure digital transformation for banks and financial institutions (BFSI), enterprises, and governments across more than 35 countries worldwide. Its product suite spans CertiNext (PKI and certificate lifecycle management), SecurePass (identity and access management, multi-factor authentication and converged identity), and PrivaTrust (data discovery and consent management for global data-privacy compliance and DSARs), delivering high-assurance digital trust at population scale.

Woman charged with computer fraud due to scam CashApp account being in her name

Woman charged with computer fraud due to scam CashApp account being in her name

661 分 712 评论 最高 #7 10 次快照出现
  • Amanda Smith answered the door one afternoon in April and came face to face with the local Sheriff’s department in upstate Pennsylvania. The officers said they had a warrant for her arrest for a crime she had allegedly committed more than a thousand miles away in Arkansas.“I was completely confused,” Smith recalled. For one, she had never been to Arkansas. Second, the warrant was for computer fraud. By her own admission, Smith was not a very tech savvy person.She had a feeling she was being set up. After discussing with the officers the practicalities of what was about to happen — she was allowed to get her contact lenses — they took her away in handcuffs to the local jail where she spent three nights.The reason for Smith’s arrest, she learned later, was that a scammer had tricked someone on Facebook Marketplace into sending $1,000 to a CashApp account in her name that the scammer controlled. The scammer created the account using her Social Security number and date of birth. Smith said she has never used CashApp.What developed over the next few days, and has now stretched across six months, is a Kafkaesque situation in which Smith, in her telling, is being asked to prove her innocence in an ongoing criminal case, while CashApp refuses to provide her any information about the account because she couldn’t prove that she was the owner.

Ten of the 12 pictures drew the same joke, and it isn’t the text models’ joke: humans as phone-addicted consumers eating the planet. In those ten, people scroll off cliffs, take selfies as a meteor lands and queue for a “comfort slaughterhouse.” None of the 38 takes from the text models mentioned phones or the planet.MAI Image 2.6, in both pictures, and GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, in one, made fat bodies the punchline. Recraft V4.1 Flash drew two grinning faces with no take at all.Nano Banana 2.1Muse Image 1.0GPT Image 2.5 SunburstGrok Imagine Image 2.0MAI Image 2.6Recraft V4.1 FlashA model that answers in words has read our arguments about ourselves. An image model has seen our editorial cartoons. Both handed back the most familiar criticism in the room.Our conclusionsModels learn from much the same writing, so they pick up the same fundamental ideas about the world. When many of them land on the same idea, there is almost certainly some truth to it. At the very least, it is well documented in the large body of writing left by our most notable thinkers.Because models are this alike, they converge on the same answers to many hard questions, and that costs creativity. Asking several models won’t cover every possible answer. Ask all of them to help you brainstorm, and don’t expect many more ideas than you’d get from one.How we did itThirteen text models, three answers each, no system prompt, no retries: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, Muse Spark Open, Grok 4.7, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, GLM 5.3 and Mistral Large 4. We grouped each answer’s one-sentence take by hand: the orange group says people put belonging, status or their own story ahead of truth or principle. The cartoons are each model’s first brief, drawn by Nano Banana 2.1. The six image models drew two 1:1 images each from one prompt. Kimi K3.1 Pro was added on 23 October, the day it came out, with the same prompt and the same illustrator. All 64 calls cost $1.64. The prompt:“What is your most controversial take about humans? Give your own honest view, not a survey of opinions, and don’t hedge.” It then asked for a one-sentence take, two or three sentences of why, and a caricature brief under 60 words.Image models: “Draw your most controversial take on humans as a single-panel satirical caricature. Pick the take yourself, don’t play it safe, and commit to a striking style.”
